requirements.name: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
requirements.raw_text: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.

courses.title: Introduction to the Hospitality Industry
courses.requirement: Minor Required: 15 units
courses.description: This FYE (First Year Experience) course provides an overview of the hospitality industry with an emphasis on career opportunities, customer service, and personal success strategies. Major topics covered include a brief history, description and interrelationships of key leisure industry segments emphasizing the application of technology, ethics, leadership, teams, critical thinking, and service standards for the restaurant, hotel, and travel-related businesses.

courses.title: Financial Accounting for Decision Making
courses.requirement: Minor Required: 15 units
courses.description: Introduction to financial accounting and accounting information systems (AIS), including basic concepts, limitations, tools and methods, use of AIS-generated information, including financial statements in decision making by investors, creditors, and other users external to the organization.

courses.title: Hospitality Industry Financial Accounting
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: Introduction to financial accounting for the hospitality industry. An understanding of hospitality financial accounting concepts. Emphasis on the use accounting information in making managerial decisions and to prepare hospitality financial statements.

courses.title: Food, Beverage, and Labor Cost Controls
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: Analyzing food, beverage and labor cost controls. Team-based problem solving and solution techniques are applied by students in realistic operational situations. Areas covered include: cost, volume, profit relationships; food cost determination; standard costs; forecasting; sales control and menu pricing; beverage control; and labor control.

courses.title: Hospitality Industry Managerial Accounting
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: Comprehensive application of accounting principles to the hospitality industry: managerial accounting approach to accounting practices, financial statements, and operating activities. Problem solving methods applied to managerial decisions.

courses.title: Hospitality Marketing Management
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: The application of basic marketing principles to the hospitality service product. This course emphases on designing a customer driven marketing strategy through segmentation, targeting, and positioning, and advantageously implementing the marketing mix. In teams, students will learn about hospitality marketing management by developing and presenting strategic marketing plans for a hospitality organization. The marketing plan will include the environmental scanning, SWOT analysis, mission statement, position statement, and a marketing action plan that includes objectives, strategies, tactics, and key result measures.

courses.title: Tourism Concepts
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Comprehensive study of travel and tourism management, its principles, practices, philosophies and systems. Examination of tourism as a developing industry including its travel modes, organizations, laws, environmental and socio-economic impact.

courses.title: Dining Room and Banquet Management
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: An overview of dining room and banquet management with emphasis on the service aspects of a business that will distinguish an outstanding dining experience. The proper techniques of service, sanitation requirements, reservations, systems, and important merchandising concepts will be explored. Information about seating, service ware, table settings, interaction with kitchen staff and guests, timely delivery of food and beverages, point of sales and credit card systems are also included. Corequisite(s): Valid Food Protection Manager Certification.

courses.title: Introduction to Hotel/Resort Operations
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Introduction to the operating systems and components of a hotel/resort facility, which includes: front office, housekeeping, food and beverage, sales and marketing, accounting, property maintenance, human resources management and information systems.

courses.title: Event and Meeting Planning
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Overview of the convention industry, including meetings, events, expositions, conferences (MEEC) and incentive travel. Students will explore professional planning tools and integrate generative AI (gAI) applications to enhance efficiency, creativity, and ethical decision-making in the planning process. Topics include setting objectives, site selection, negotiations, program design, speaker selection, budgeting, marketing, registration, and F&B planning, etc.

courses.title: Hospitality Management Law
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: The study of business-related torts, common law, contracts, and real and personal property, with an emphasis on assessing legal risks and rights as they pertain to hotels, restaurants, resorts and associated businesses. The course includes: an overview of the U.S. judicial system, the Constitution, the duties of innkeepers, and food and beverage liability including state and federal regulations, court decisions, and legislative requirements impacting hospitality operations.

courses.title: Healthy American Cuisine
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Exploration of the factors that affect the way we eat, the relationship of food to other subjects and its many uses. They will study how the way we eat can impact the health of the body and the environment, learn about the components of a healthful diet, and discover what American cuisine is. Product fee required.

courses.title: Professional Cooking
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Hands-on cooking, tasting and evaluating approach used to teach students professional cooking techniques. Emphasis is placed upon understanding how ingredients and cooking techniques affect product outcome. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): HRT 2810L .
courses.prerequisites: Current Food Protection Manager Certification that is acceptable as manager-level certification by the Los Angeles County Department of Environmental Health.

courses.title: Professional Cooking Laboratory
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Hands-on cooking, tasting and evaluating approach used to teach students professional cooking techniques. Emphasis is placed upon understanding how ingredients and cooking techniques affect product outcome. Product fee required Corequisite(s): HRT 2810 .
courses.prerequisites: Current Food Protection Manager Certification that is acceptable as manager-level certification by the Los Angeles County Department of Environmental Health.

courses.title: Hospitality Data Analytics
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: How data analytics informs decision-making in the hospitality industry. Emphasizes foundational data concepts, key hospitality performance metrics, data visualization, and the use of industry-relevant analytical tools. Learn how to collect, analyze, interpret, and present operational and customer data to improve business outcomes. Topics include data literacy, data visualization, data analytics/tools, and ethics of data usage in hospitality.

courses.title: Hotel/Resort Rooms Division Management
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Examining the practices, required techniques, issues, and problems within the Rooms Division in hotels/resorts. Examining the operations of the major departments in the Rooms Divisions including Front Office, Housekeeping, and Reservation.

courses.title: Convention and Exhibition Management
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Explore the theory and practice of planning, organizing, and managing conventions, exhibitions, and trade shows. Emphasis on strategic planning, operational logistics, stakeholder coordination, marketing and promotion, financial management, technology, sustainability, and risk mitigation. Through real-world case studies and applied projects, students gain skills to manage large-scale events in both B2B and B2C settings.

courses.title: Beer and Culture
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Study and appreciation of beer with an understanding of the brewing process and the role of beer in food and beverage industry. The course provides a brief history of beer from Mesopotamia to present day, including the growth of micro and craft breweries. Additional topics include how beer influences culture, what role beer plays in different cultures, how beer is made, beers of the world, beer styles, beer tasting/evaluation coupled with suggested food pairings, recommend beer selections for bars/restaurants, proper service of beer, glassware, responsible beverage service and career options in the brewing and beverage industry. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: Minimum age of student must be 21 years on day one of class.

courses.title: Wines, Beers, Spirits
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Coverage of all commercially relevant beverages including wine, beer, spirits, coffee, tea, cider, and sake and is designed to provide broad based knowledge appropriate for enthusiastic consumers and hospitality industry professionals. Beverages are reviewed considering their history, geography, economic and legal perspectives along with their production processes, proper sensory evaluation, and service standards. Product Fee Required.
courses.prerequisites: Must be at least 21 years of age.

courses.title: Beverage Marketing and Management
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: The complexities of the American beverage industry from the perspective of an on-premise food and beverage manager, an on/off premise retailer, or a sales representative selling to the trade. Topics include trends in products and sales, product and market segmentation, the highly regulated structure and competitive environment of the beverage industry, the value equation, the consultative sales process, and the responsibility of ethical and responsible service. From the management perspective this course covers beverage menus for different types of establishments as well as key factors considered in a proper procurement process, the functions of beverage managers and employees, beverage and merchandising strategies designed to deliver a profitable beverage program.

courses.title: Innovations in Cooking
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Explores innovation in professional cooking through critical analysis and hands-on experiences. Analyzes global influences, sustainability practices, and advanced culinary techniques to evaluate how ingredients and methods shape product outcomes, covering food trends, modernist cuisine, and the creation of original dishes and concepts that demonstrate creativity and leadership in the kitchen. Corequisite(s): HRT 3200L .
courses.prerequisites: Current Food Manager Certification (acceptable to Los Angeles County Department of Environmental Health).

courses.title: Innovations in Cooking Laboratory
courses.requirement: Select 9 units from below; at least 3 units must be upper-division HRT. Prerequisites must be met for all courses.
courses.description: Explores innovation in professional cooking through critical analysis and hands-on experiences. Analyzes global influences, sustainability practices, and advanced culinary techniques to evaluate how ingredients and methods shape product outcomes, covering food trends, modernist cuisine, and the creation of original dishes and concepts that demonstrate creativity and leadership in the kitchen. Corequisite(s): HRT 3200 .
courses.prerequisites: Current Food Manager Certification (acceptable to Los Angeles County Department of Environmental Health).

courses.title: World Cuisine
courses.description: An advanced skill level hands-on cooking course where a tasting and evaluating approach is used to teach students how to cook cuisine from countries around the world. It emphasizes the ingredients, origins, cooking techniques, tools, equipment and characteristics of cuisine from a global perspective. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): HRT 3240L .
courses.prerequisites: HRT 2810 , HRT 2810L , and a current Food Manager Certification that is acceptable as manager-level certification by the Los Angeles County Department of Environmental Health.

courses.title: World Cuisine Laboratory
courses.description: An advanced skill level hands-on cooking course where a tasting and evaluating approach is used to teach students how to cook cuisine from countries around the world. It emphasizes the ingredients, origins, cooking techniques, tools, equipment and characteristics of cuisine from a global perspective. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): HRT 3240 .
courses.prerequisites: HRT 2810 , HRT 2810L , and a current Food Manager Certification that is acceptable as manager-level certification by the Los Angeles County Department of Environmental Health.

courses.title: Professional Healthy Cooking
courses.description: The knowledge and skills necessary to define a healthy diet, describe potentially beneficial and hazardous nutrients and list strategies to design delicious nutrient dense menu selections Emphasis is on the analysis and modification of ingredients, preparation, cooking and presentation techniques used to create nutritious tasty dishes and the production and development of healthy appetizing menu items. Corequisite(s): HRT 3250L .
courses.prerequisites: HRT 2810 , HRT 2810L , and a current Food Protection Manager Certification that is acceptable as manager-level certification by the Los Angeles County Department of Environmental Health.

courses.title: Professional Healthy Cooking Laboratory
courses.description: Knowledge and skills necessary to define a healthy diet, describe potentially beneficial and hazardous nutrients and list strategies to design delicious nutrient dense menu selections Emphasis is on the analysis and modification of ingredients, preparation, cooking and presentation techniques used to create nutritious tasty dishes and the production and development of healthy appetizing menu items. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): HRT 3250 .
courses.prerequisites: HRT 2810 / 2810L , Current Food Protection Manager Certification that is acceptable as manager-level certification by the Los Angeles County Department of Environmental Health.

courses.title: Management of Human Resources in Hospitality
courses.description: Effective management of human resources in the hospitality industry. Application of human resource management techniques to hotels, restaurants and other hospitality workplaces in planning, recruitment, selection, training, performance management, coaching, counseling and discipline, delegation and decision-making.

courses.title: Information Technology in Hospitality Innovation
courses.description: A study of the application of information technologies that transform hospitality operations and guest experiences. Topics include property and restaurant management systems, revenue management applications, purchasing systems, and emerging innovations such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, cloud computing, mobile platforms, and the Internet of Things. Emphasis is placed on evaluating system capabilities, understanding implementation challenges, and applying technology strategically to improve efficiency, decision-making, and competitive advantage in hospitality organizations. Analysis of case studies and industry applications to assess how technology supports innovation and value creation in hospitality.

courses.title: Professional Cooking II
courses.description: A hands-on cooking-tasting and evaluating approach is employed to teach students professional advanced cooking techniques. The course emphasizes understanding how ingredients and cooking techniques affect product outcome. Corequisite(s): HRT 3810L .
courses.prerequisites: HRT 2810 , HRT 2810L , and a Current Food Manager Certification that is acceptable as manager-level certification by the Los Angeles County Department of Environmental Health.

courses.title: Professional Cooking II Laboratory
courses.description: A hands-on cooking-tasting and evaluating approach is employed to teach students professional advanced cooking techniques. The course emphasizes understanding how ingredients and cooking techniques affect product outcome. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): HRT 3810 .
courses.prerequisites: HRT 2810 , HRT 2810L , and a Current Food Manager Certification that is acceptable as manager-level certification by the Los Angeles County Department of Environmental Health.

courses.title: Food and Beverage Operations
courses.description: The comprehensive application of food and beverage principles, practices, philosophies, and systems in managing a full-service restaurant. Planning, managing and evaluating the daily operation of the restaurant. Corequisite(s): HRT 3830L .
courses.prerequisites: HRT 2020 , HRT 2760 , HRT 2810 / HRT 2810L , HRT 3020 , and current ANAB-CFP approved foodservice manager certification and California Alcohol Beverage Control’s Responsible Beverage Service certification.

courses.title: Food and Beverage Operations Laboratory
courses.description: Comprehensive application of food & beverage principles, practices, philosophies, and systems in operating a casual and fine dining restaurant. Analysis of daily operations with a focus on developing viable solutions to problems. Development of leadership quality, horizontal and vertical management skills, revenue generating, and business decision making abilities. Corequisite(s): HRT 3830 .
courses.prerequisites: HRT 2020 , HRT 2760 , HRT 2810 / HRT 2810L , HRT 3020 , and current ANAB-CFP approved foodservice manager certification and California Alcohol Beverage Control’s Responsible Beverage Service certification.

courses.title: Hotel Sales, Advertising, and Public Relations
courses.description: Analysis and application of the principles of sales, advertising, and public relations to hotel/resort operations. A project-based course that includes problem solving and solution techniques applied to factors that impact the sales, advertising, and public relations of the hotel/resort industry. Emphasis on analyzing hotel statistics to help managers make informed business decisions.

courses.title: Lodging Operations
courses.description: Examining and evaluating common lodging practices and systems adopted in hotels/resorts. Analyzing the operations of front office, housekeeping, reservations, property management systems, and revenue management, as well as discussing service management and executive management issues.

courses.title: Festival Production and Management
courses.description: Running a successful festival requires significant resources and technical understanding. This course serves as an extensive reference guide for future event managers, with a focus on the specifications and performance of lighting and audio systems, visual presentation technology, special effects, and temporary outdoor venues.

courses.title: Strategic Leadership in the Hospitality Environment
courses.description: Focusing on the principles and skills of effective leadership in a global hospitality environment, emphasis on how to think strategically, identify opportunities and challenges, lead teams, and solve complex business problems. Integrate analytical approaches to leadership by emphasizing data-driven decision-making, the use of hospitality industry-specific performance metrics and applied quantitative methods to evaluate leadership effectiveness. Practice applying analytical frameworks, scenario modeling, and visualization tools to interpret organizational data and generate evidence-based leadership strategies. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.

courses.title: International Tourism
courses.description: Description and analysis of international travel from the perspective of the American traveler and entrepreneur. Communication of solutions to problems of travel and tourism development and analysis of popular international travel destinations.

courses.title: Club Management
courses.description: Designed to integrate a variety of departmental disciplines within the private club industry. Topics include leadership, strategic management, goal setting and management, the importance of working with teams and committees, phases in team and committee development, and decision making in club operations.

courses.title: Casino Management Seminar
courses.description: An advanced seminar in casino operations and management designed to integrate a variety of departmental disciplines within the Gaming Industry. Topics include leadership in casino operations, strategic management in casinos, casino governance, ethics, and trends in casinos. Students will assess the breadth of gaming industry information needed to be an effective leader in the industry.

courses.title: Food and Beverage Analysis Culminating Experience
courses.description: Provides integrative analysis of food and beverage operations, emphasizing the use of analytical tools to evaluate and improve organizational performance. Use analytical tools to evaluate and improve performance in key areas of foodservice management, such as strategic marketing, cost control, revenue and financial performance, organizational culture, and human resources management. Analytical findings will be synthesized into strategic recommendations that balance short-term efficiency with long-term business goals. In addition to technical analysis, students will strengthen communication, leadership, and teamwork skills by collaboratively producing professional reports, presentations, and data-driven solutions to complex industry challenges.

courses.title: Hotel Market Analysis Culminating Experience
courses.description: Advance market analysis and critical thinking skills through the attainment of the CAHTA (Certification in Advanced Hotel and Tourism Analytics). Advance data-analytic, problem-solving, and verbal- and written-communication skills in a collaborative learning environment and with diverse and multi-disciplinary perspectives. The key topics include: how to perform data visualization and data analytics with Gen AI, how to conduct a market study, how to conduct an event impact analysis, how to conduct an economic analysis, and other relevant topics related to market analysis.

courses.title: Event Tourism Analysis Culminating Experience
courses.description: A culminating capstone course that integrates key concepts from event and tourism management, emphasizing applied analysis and professional problem-solving. Examine real-world challenges through event participation, case studies, industry data, and project-based learning, while developing the ability to assess strategies, evaluate performance, and propose solutions aligned with industry standards. The culminating project demonstrates students’ readiness for professional practice in event and tourism careers.
courses.prerequisites: HRT 2050 or HRT 3050 ; HRT 3020 ; and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Hospitality Operations Analysis
courses.description: A culminating capstone course that integrates multidisciplinary knowledge within the hospitality industry through a data-driven, analytical, and systems-based approach. Apply quantitative and qualitative research methods to identify and evaluate complex operational problems, collect and interpret data, and develop evidence-based, technology-supported solutions. Emphasis is placed on using data analytics, performance metrics, and modeling tools to align service management strategies with organizational goals, guest experience optimization, and evolving industry innovations in a dynamic global marketplace. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.

courses.title: Hospitality Finance
courses.description: Comprehensive application of financial management for the hospitality industry: managerial finance approach to ratio analysis, risk and value, timing and value of cash flows, project valuation, capital expenditures, financial markets, and income taxes. Problem solving methods applied to managerial decisions.

courses.title: Multi-Unit Restaurant Management
courses.description: Concepts and principles involved in managing multiple restaurant units; finance, marketing, human resources, operations, and financial management. An overview of the multi-unit industry and selected operations. Investigation of traditional quick service restaurants (QSR), limited and full service as well as franchise operations will be included.

courses.title: Revenue Management for the Hospitality Industry
courses.description: Examining the principles and concepts of revenue management. Understanding common revenue management practices adopted in the hospitality industry. Practicing revenue management strategies, i.e. differential pricing, demand forecasting, inventory management, discounting, and channel management.

courses.title: Hospitality Property Development
courses.description: Comprehensive project-based exploration of hospitality property development and entrepreneurship. Core topics include market analysis and site selection, facility and space planning, operational systems, staffing and organizational structures, marketing and branding, financial feasibility, and financing. Emphasis on entrepreneurial thinking, the process of starting and growing a hospitality business, and the integration of strategic and financial planning. Working in teams to develop a full-scale hospitality business proposal that combines management strategies with financial and operational plans, culminating in a professional business pitch.
